text: In the heterogeneous III-V-on-silicon approach (the Fang/Bowers insight), unpatterned III-V films are bonded to silicon and the laser cavity is defined afterward by silicon lithography. Why is this decisive over flip-chip die bonding?
choices: It eliminates the need for III-V material entirely
It lets the laser operate without electrical pumping
Because the cavity is defined lithographically after bonding, die-placement precision becomes irrelevant — enabling wafer-scale (Intel-scale) production
It removes all coupling loss between the laser and the silicon waveguide
explanation: Bonding a blank III-V film and then patterning it with silicon lithography means the sub-micron placement burden vanishes (placement precision becomes irrelevant), which is what enables high-volume manufacturing. Choice 0 is wrong — gain still needs III-V; choice 1 is false (the laser is still electrically pumped); choice 3 overstates it — coupling loss is engineered down but not eliminated.
